description: Each invoice's ratio is the mean of its line-level total-cost ÷ unit-price ratios.

b.request: For each invoice, calculate the mean of (derived_total_cost / product_price) across its line items; calculate the overall mean of these per-invoice means; filter to invoices where the per-invoice mean exceeds this overall mean; and report the mean derived_product_cost across all line items in filtered invoices, the mean per-invoice ratio for filtered invoices, and the mean excess of filtered invoices' ratios above the overall mean ratio.
b.sql:
WITH invoice_ratios AS (
  SELECT 
    invoice_number,
    AVG(derived_total_cost / NULLIF(product_price, 0)) as per_invoice_mean_ratio
  FROM Invoice_Line_Items
  WHERE product_price IS NOT NULL AND product_price != 0
  GROUP BY invoice_number
),
overall_mean_cte AS (
  SELECT AVG(per_invoice_mean_ratio) as overall_mean_ratio
  FROM invoice_ratios
),
filtered_invoices AS (
  SELECT ir.invoice_number, ir.per_invoice_mean_ratio
  FROM invoice_ratios ir
  CROSS JOIN overall_mean_cte om
  WHERE ir.per_invoice_mean_ratio > om.overall_mean_ratio
)
SELECT 
  (SELECT AVG(ili.derived_product_cost) 
   FROM Invoice_Line_Items ili 
   WHERE ili.invoice_number IN (SELECT invoice_number FROM filtered_invoices)) as mean_derived_product_cost,
  (SELECT AVG(per_invoice_mean_ratio) FROM filtered_invoices) as mean_per_invoice_ratio,
  (SELECT AVG(fi.per_invoice_mean_ratio - om.overall_mean_ratio) 
   FROM filtered_invoices fi 
   CROSS JOIN overall_mean_cte om) as mean_excess
b.raw: For each invoice, calculate the mean of (derived_total_cost / product_price) across its line items; calculate the overall mean of these per-invoice means; filter to invoices where the per-invoice mean exceeds this overall mean; and report the mean derived_product_cost across all line items in filtered invoices, the mean per-invoice ratio for filtered invoices, and the mean excess of filtered invoices' ratios above the overall mean ratio.

a.request: For each invoice (`Invoice_Line_Items.invoice_number`), take the average line product cost (`derived_product_cost`). Also take its total-cost-to-price ratio, found by dividing each line's `derived_total_cost` by its `product_price` and averaging those line ratios. Missing values are ignored. Average the invoice ratios across all invoices, and keep only the invoices whose ratio is above that average. As a single row, report the average over the kept invoices of (1) their average line product cost, (2) their ratio, and (3) how far their ratio exceeds the overall average ratio. Don't round.
a.sql: WITH invoice_stats AS (SELECT invoice_number, AVG(derived_product_cost) as avg_product_cost, AVG(CASE WHEN product_price IS NOT NULL AND product_price != 0 AND derived_total_cost IS NOT NULL THEN derived_total_cost / product_price ELSE NULL END) as invoice_ratio FROM Invoice_Line_Items GROUP BY invoice_number), overall_avg AS (SELECT AVG(invoice_ratio) as overall_ratio FROM invoice_stats) SELECT AVG(stats.avg_product_cost) as avg_line_product_cost, AVG(stats.invoice_ratio) as avg_invoice_ratio, AVG(stats.invoice_ratio) - overall.overall_ratio as ratio_exceeds_average FROM invoice_stats stats CROSS JOIN overall_avg overall WHERE stats.invoice_ratio > overall.overall_ratio

d.request: For each invoice, calculate the mean derived_product_cost and mean (derived_total_cost / product_price) ratio across its line items; select invoices exceeding the overall mean ratio; output the mean product cost, mean ratio, and the excess of their mean ratio over the overall mean ratio for these selected invoices.
d.sql: WITH invoice_metrics AS (SELECT invoice_number, AVG(derived_product_cost) as mean_product_cost, AVG(derived_total_cost / product_price) as mean_ratio FROM Invoice_Line_Items GROUP BY invoice_number), overall_mean_ratio AS (SELECT AVG(derived_total_cost / product_price) as overall_mean_ratio FROM Invoice_Line_Items) SELECT im.invoice_number, im.mean_product_cost, im.mean_ratio, im.mean_ratio - omr.overall_mean_ratio as excess_ratio FROM invoice_metrics im CROSS JOIN overall_mean_ratio omr WHERE im.mean_ratio > omr.overall_mean_ratio

c.request: For each invoice, look at its average line product cost (`derived_product_cost`) and its ratio of total cost (`derived_total_cost`) to unit price (`product_price`), ignoring missing values. Take the invoices whose ratio is above the average ratio across all invoices. In a single row, what are their average product cost, their average ratio, and on average how far their ratio sits above that overall average? No rounding. Each invoice's ratio is the mean of its line-level total-cost ÷ unit-price ratios.
c.sql:
WITH line_ratios AS (
  SELECT 
    invoice_number,
    derived_product_cost,
    CASE 
      WHEN product_price IS NOT NULL 
        AND product_price != 0 
        AND derived_total_cost IS NOT NULL 
      THEN derived_total_cost / product_price 
      ELSE NULL 
    END as ratio
  FROM Invoice_Line_Items
),
invoice_stats AS (
  SELECT 
    invoice_number,
    AVG(derived_product_cost) as avg_product_cost,
    AVG(ratio) as avg_ratio
  FROM line_ratios
  GROUP BY invoice_number
),
filtered_invoices AS (
  SELECT 
    i.avg_product_cost,
    i.avg_ratio
  FROM invoice_stats i
  WHERE i.avg_ratio > (SELECT AVG(avg_ratio) FROM invoice_stats)
)
SELECT 
  AVG(avg_product_cost) as avg_product_cost,
  AVG(avg_ratio) as avg_ratio,
  AVG(avg_ratio) - (SELECT AVG(avg_ratio) FROM invoice_stats) as avg_ratio_above_overall
FROM filtered_invoices
